podcast.title: Critically Praised and Influential
podcast.body: Huggy Bear was part of the riot grrrl scene, which, though not commercially successful, garnered critical praise and was highly influential for subsequent generations of bands. "There were groups like Huggy Barred."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Breakup
podcast.body: By 1994, Huggy Bear had broken up, mirroring the fate of other original Riot Grrrl bands like Bratmobile and Heavens to Betsy. This breakup was attributed to the intense, political, and emotional nature of the scene, which could not be sustained long-term. "By 1994, Brad Mabel, Evans De Betsy and Huggy Bear had all broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: London-based Riot Grrrl with Male Members
podcast.body: Huggy Bear was a Riot Grrrl band from London that uniquely included a couple of guys in the band, with one of the male members occasionally singing lead. This differentiated them from the predominantly all-female Riot Grrrl groups in the American Pacific Northwest. "Huggy Bear was from London and differentiated itself by having a couple of guys in the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Huggy Bear is mentioned as one of the bands within the Riot Grrrl movement. "And then there were bands like Sugar Baby Doll and the Pagan Babies and Brat Mobio and Heaven's De Betsy and Huggy Bear."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Breakup
xref.body: By 1994, Bratmobile had broken up. This was part of the general decline of the original Riot Grrrl scene due to various internal and external pressures, including conflicting ideas about media coverage and the co-option of "girl power." "By 1994, Brad Mabel, Evans De Betsy and Huggy Bear had all broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Breakup
xref.body: By 1994, Heavens to Betsy had broken up. This dissolution was part of the broader end of the original Riot Grrrl scene, influenced by differing views on media exposure and the watering down of its "girl power" ideals. "By 1994, Brad Mabel, Evans De Betsy and Huggy Bear had all broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Longevity of Original Riot Grrrl Bands
xref.body: Bikini Kill was the only original Riot Grrrl band to continue performing beyond the mid-90s, lasting until 1997. Most other early bands like Bratmobile, Heavens to Betsy, and Huggy Bear had broken up by 1994 due to internal conflicts and issues surrounding media coverage. "The only original Riot Girl band to make it beyond all that was Bikini Kill. They lasted until 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
